title: Letting Someone Else Carry Part of It

beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: Dave lays three cards down. "Let's see if reaching out actually undoes anything."

beats.prompt: The past: the old habits you finally cut loose.
The present: the chain you decided to lift on your own.
The future: reaching back out instead of carrying it all alone.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Okay, quiz me. Doesn't reaching out for help kind of undo the whole point of finally deciding things myself?"

options.text: No — asking for help isn't handing the decision back to someone else.
It does — you should've just kept doing it alone.
The Star doesn't apply to asking for help at all.

elaboration: The Star's light is a quietly nonconformist one — hope that doesn't need everyone else's approval, which isn't the same as needing no one's help at all.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "What if I ask for help and it turns out to be a total waste of everyone's time?"

options.text: Even a small ask can end up feeding something bigger than you expect.
Then you'll have wasted their time for nothing.
Asking for help is never actually worth it.

elaboration: An act of giving that seems small can nourish something a lot larger than it looks like from where you're standing.

beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: "One thread ties all three: what you cut away, the habit you finally set down, and the people you're letting back in to help carry the rest."

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Yeah. I think I mistook 'doing it myself' for 'doing it alone.' Those aren't the same thing. Thanks — really."
